key_insight: A computational search identified 58 CuI-based ternary candidates for p-type transparent conductors and generalized design rules beyond oxide materials.
engineering_relevance: These materials could expand transparent hole-conducting options for tandem photovoltaics and transparent electronics, pending experimental validation.
method: Search X–Cu–I structures using minima hopping and density functional theory.
Filter for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Analyze Cu coordination and electronic structure to refine chemical modulation of the valence band design rules.
evidence_signal: The search yielded 58 candidates, including 49 previously unreported compounds and 20 predicted p-type degenerate semiconductors; Cu₂FI₂ has a calculated 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m₀ hole effective mass.
watch_item: Computational screening does not establish synthesizability, measured transparency or conductivity, or compatibility with solar-cell fabrication.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
